evidence.exact_quote: A doc that consumes orchestration, routing, runtime identity, approval, or worktree/lane behavior must consume the owning contract rather than restating feature-local canon.

items.impact: Establishes the document-wide anti-drift invariant used by all atomized rules.
items.statement: Consumer plans reference owner canon and cannot create feature-local peer canon.
items.title: Document-wide owner-consumption invariant

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: DRY_Rules.md is the canonical DRY/SSOT rule owner; platform naming is "Puppet Master" only, and older names may be referenced only as "legacy naming" without quoting them.

items.impact: Prevents naming drift and accidental revival of retired names.
items.statement: DRY_Rules is the owner and only the Puppet Master name is canonical.
items.title: Canonical naming authority

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: DRY rules define how plan documents reference SSOT sources instead of duplicating them, and how ContractRef annotations make requirements executable and gateable.

items.impact: Makes owner references and requirement traceability explicit plan-quality inputs.
items.statement: The DRY mechanism combines SSOT reference discipline with gateable ContractRef annotations.
items.title: Anti-drift scope and traceability

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When documents conflict, resolution order is Spec_Lock.json, Crosswalk.md, DRY_Rules.md, Glossary.md, then Decision_Policy.md.

items.impact: Provides a deterministic authority order for conflicting plan statements.
items.statement: Conflict resolution follows a fixed five-source precedence chain.
items.title: Global SSOT precedence

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Consumer docs for orchestration, routing, runtime identity, approval, or worktree/lane behavior consume owning contracts instead of restating feature-local canon.

items.impact: Keeps high-risk runtime and approval semantics synchronized with their owners.
items.statement: Named consumer families must consume, not restate, owning contracts.
items.title: Owner contract consumption

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Owner docs update before consumers; stale canonical text is replaced or retired; older models cannot remain peer options once replacement canon exists.

items.impact: Defines propagation order and removes misleading stale alternatives.
items.statement: Canon changes propagate owner-first and retire displaced models rather than appending around them.
items.title: Owner-first reconciliation

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Summary, checklist, feature-list, newtools, newfeatures, MCP origin, Firecrawl/lost-spec, reference, promoted-feature, approval ladder, and HITL material remain consumer alignment only and must reconcile after owner changes.

items.impact: Prevents summaries and intake-origin material from masquerading as current owner canon.
items.statement: Mirror and origin surfaces are consumers that require reconciliation after owner changes.
items.title: Consumer mirror alignment

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Blocked-episode approval identity, requested/effective runtime identity, account binding, retry/account-switch, route_target, OpenSubject, route/open-by-identity, lane/worktree, thread-worktree, concern, and graph-generation/patch concepts are owner-routed and must not be re-owned by consumers.

items.impact: Protects identity, approval, routing, worktree, and lineage boundaries from divergent consumer schemas.
items.statement: The enumerated cross-cutting concept families remain owner-routed.
items.title: Owner-routed concept families

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Executor owns ready-set/backoff/remediation scheduling, Contracts owns runtime event and payload vocabulary, chain-wizard-flexibility owns wizard_status, and legacy NEEDS/RECONCILIATION are transfer-state dispositions, not live enum values.

items.impact: Separates scheduler behavior, event vocabulary, wizard state, and legacy audit dispositions.
items.statement: Runtime scheduling and blocked-state concepts have distinct owners and legacy audit flags are not runtime states.
items.title: Runtime scheduling owner route

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run_Graph_View owns graph inspector and /full-record presentation, Contracts owns concern/promotion/graph-patch/recovery contracts, storage owns investigation/storage wire formats, and UI_Command_Catalog owns wrapper-command normalization.

items.impact: Prevents graph UI, runtime records, persistence, and command wrappers from re-owning one another.
items.statement: Graph presentation, record contracts, storage formats, and command normalization are explicitly separated.
items.title: Graph record storage boundary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Compare/open identity, hunk controls, diff-local search, cross-surface receipts, Orchestrator run-to-repo lineage, Health read-only posture, and Source Control live-worktree truth stay with their owner docs.

items.impact: Maintains consistent compare, review, lineage, health, and source-control truth across GUI surfaces.
items.statement: Compare/review/SC responsibilities remain with their named owners.
items.title: Compare and SCM boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: owner_node_id is canonical for worktree orchestration-node lineage, while owner_tier_id may remain only as documented compatibility, migration, or source-lineage evidence beside owner_node_id.

items.impact: Makes the canonical lineage field unambiguous while bounding legacy compatibility.
items.statement: owner_node_id is canonical and owner_tier_id is compatibility-only beside it.
items.title: Worktree owner-node compatibility

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Permissions_System owns permission snapshot schema, enums, approval-surface expectations, and blocked-action semantics; storage owns only durable binding keys and cannot redefine nested permission snapshot schema.

items.impact: Avoids permission-semantic drift between authorization and persistence layers.
items.statement: Permission schema semantics and storage bindings have separate owners.
items.title: Permission snapshot ownership split

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Special recovery contradiction checks are DRY-routing evidence, not new ownership assignments, and adjacent contradiction review stays routed through the named owner docs.

items.impact: Stops recovery audits from silently reallocating canonical ownership.
items.statement: Recovery contradiction checks supply routing evidence only; they do not assign ownership.
items.title: Recovery routing is not ownership

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Tooling and memory consumer checks keep named docs as contradiction-review inputs only and do not let consumer summaries re-own schema, command, runtime, permission, or storage canon.

items.impact: Preserves owner authority when tooling and memory documents are used as audit inputs.
items.statement: Tooling and memory consumers are contradiction inputs, not alternate schema owners.
items.title: Consumer checks remain non-authoritative

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Audit-overlap and contract checks reconcile owner docs before consumer docs, preserve stricter ContractRef taxonomy in gate text, and treat duplicate/stale text as DRY reconciliation risk.

items.impact: Aligns audit repair order with authority and keeps gates stricter than summaries.
items.statement: Audits reconcile owners first and do not let consumer summaries weaken gate taxonomy.
items.title: Audit and contract-check ordering

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: projection-backed operational surfaces expose trust state, last updated time, degraded or /stale reason when not current, and whether actions are partially gated.

items.impact: Different builders can choose incompatible freshness thresholds, trust-state values, stale transitions, gating behavior, and assistive text, allowing the same projection to appear trustworthy or actionable on one surface and degraded on another.
items.statement: The required projection disclosures are named, but their state vocabulary, freshness oracle, transition rules, exact partial-action gates, offline behavior, accessibility announcement, localization, and support telemetry are not specified here.
items.title: Projection trust state lacks a testable UI state machine

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Early event-source tables that already consume newer runtime-lineage concepts are internally stale and duplicated Crosswalk numbering is a DRY failure undermining ContractRef stability and traceability.

items.impact: Classifies two concrete traceability failures that must be repaired at their owner route.
items.statement: Internally stale event tables and duplicated Crosswalk numbering are explicit DRY failures.
items.title: Stale event and Crosswalk integrity

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Corroboration routing keeps corroboration_request input and corroboration_result output evidence distinct, while dispatch contracts separate mandatory executor-facing fields from optional disclosure or /overlay fields.

items.impact: Without an owner-bound field list and rejection oracle, dispatchers can disagree on correctness-critical input, optional overlays can accidentally become required, and malformed packets can fail only after execution begins.
items.statement: The request/result and mandatory/optional boundaries are explicit, but this unit does not identify the mandatory executor fields, schema owner, validation timing, or failure response.
items.title: Corroboration dispatch boundary is not independently falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI /behavior docs need owner-defined operational policy before consumer summaries can be canonical, and route reconciliation updates owner docs before consumers consume the canonical route/object model.

items.impact: Prevents GUI summaries from inventing route or identity behavior before owner policy exists.
items.statement: UI behavior and route/object identity remain consumer views of owner-defined operational policy.
items.title: UI behavior and route reconciliation

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: assistant-chat-design owns assistant worktree binding, seglog events, commands, settings, merge-back flow, and pre-merge test gate, while GitHub_Integration and storage-plan own SC accordion and owner_thread_id boundaries.

items.impact: Assigns assistant-worktree behavior, GUI layout, and stored lineage to distinct owners.
items.statement: Assistant worktree behavior belongs to assistant-chat-design, with bounded GitHub and storage ownership.
items.title: Assistant worktree owner routes

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Consumer docs must cross-reference assistant worktree owners rather than redefining canonical tables, enums, field lists, or behavioral rules.

items.impact: Eliminates duplicate assistant-worktree schema and behavior definitions.
items.statement: Assistant worktree consumers cross-reference owners and do not redefine canonical details.
items.title: Assistant worktree consumer cross-references

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: assistant-chat-design owns chat/runtime/question/dispatcher behavior and consumer carry-through points for web, permissions, runtime identity, blocked payloads, and TODO persistence.

items.impact: Keeps chat dispatcher and downstream web, permission, identity, blocked, and TODO behavior coherent.
items.statement: assistant-chat-design owns the chat/runtime/question/dispatcher seam and its carry-through behavior.
items.title: Assistant chat dispatcher owner route

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Assistant chat traceability preserves named carry-through anchors, /runtime/question/dispatcher owner seam, /section metadata, and the listed obligation IDs.

items.impact: Retains stable anchors and obligation identifiers for cross-document verification.
items.statement: Named anchors, section metadata, owner seam, and obligation IDs are preserved as traceability inputs.
items.title: Assistant chat traceability anchors

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Plans may include index/list material for event kinds, UI command IDs, or tool IDs, but must not redefine schemas owned elsewhere.

items.impact: Allows discoverability without transferring schema ownership.
items.statement: Index-only ID lists are permitted so long as they do not redefine owner schemas.
items.title: Index-only lists are bounded consumers

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Plan requirements forbid TBD, Open question, ask later, vague unmeasurable adjectives, and duplicated provider CLI details outside Provider SSOT.

items.impact: A literal scanner may flag quoted examples, code, historical text, or localized prose, while a semantic reviewer may inconsistently decide what is vague or measurable.
items.statement: The forbidden tokens and vague-adjective policy are clear, but scope exclusions, matching rules, localization handling, and the measurable pass/fail oracle are not defined in this unit.
items.title: Forbidden-pattern detection lacks exact matching semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Any statement using MUST, SHALL, REQUIRED, or NEVER must include at least one ContractRef line.

items.impact: Creates a mechanically recognizable trigger for required traceability.
items.statement: Normative keyword use requires at least one ContractRef line.
items.title: ContractRef required keywords

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Allowed ContractRef categories are SchemaID, ContractName, Primitive, ToolID, EventType, ConfigKey, PolicyRule, UICommand, Invariant, and Gate.

items.impact: Bounds the ContractRef namespace for deterministic validation.
items.statement: ContractRef entries use one of ten allowed category prefixes.
items.title: ContractRef taxonomy

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Every operational requirement must have at least one ContractRef, detected deterministically by MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, REQUIRED, or NEVER, while preserving the path-plus-anchor example format.

items.impact: Defines both the trigger vocabulary and the traceability-format expectation.
items.statement: Operational requirement detection is keyword-based and requires a ContractRef with preserved path-plus-anchor form.
items.title: Operational requirement annotation rule

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: VERIFIER packet preflight and SCRIBE self-check strip standalone ContractRef lines, normalize CRLF/LF, whitespace, and blank lines, and must not weaken ContractRef enforcement in run-gates or other plan-quality gates.

items.impact: Whitespace-significant code, tables, YAML, or string literals can normalize to the same text even when their semantics differ, producing false-positive packet fidelity unless the matching domain or collision oracle is constrained.
items.statement: The six-step semantic normalization is deterministic, but this unit does not define exclusions or collision detection for whitespace-significant canonical content.
items.title: Packet normalization can erase semantic distinctions

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: References should prefer canonical files/anchors and stable anchors over inline duplication or unstable heading slug references.

items.impact: Builders and reviewers can disagree about when a stable anchor is required, so link stability is not mechanically enforceable from this unit alone.
items.statement: Reference style is expressed as a preference without a threshold or rejection condition.
items.title: Reference-style guidance is not gateable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Operational requirements without ContractRef are non-canonical and must fail the plan-quality gate.

items.impact: Defines the required failure outcome for missing operational traceability.
items.statement: An operational requirement without ContractRef is non-canonical and fails the plan-quality gate.
items.title: Unreferenced operational text fails

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Inline requirement tags such as Req:FR-001, Req:NFR-001, and Req:REQ-001 are readability-only and do not constitute traceability evidence.

items.impact: Prevents convenient prose tags from being mistaken for authoritative requirement coverage.
items.statement: Req-prefixed inline tags are readability aids only.
items.title: Inline requirement tags are non-authoritative

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Authoritative requirement coverage lives only in node shard requirement_refs fields and derived .puppet-master/project/traceability/requirements_coverage.json.

items.impact: During pre-node planning phases, neither named authority may exist, leaving no stated authoritative representation for requirement coverage and inviting premature or inconsistent coverage claims.
items.statement: The two authoritative coverage surfaces are explicit, but the contract does not state the pre-node behavior when node shards and derived coverage JSON have not yet been created.
items.title: Requirement coverage authority has no pre-node state

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Inline tags must not be the sole traceability mechanism, and when an inline tag conflicts with a node requirement_refs value, requirement_refs is authoritative.

items.impact: Supplies an explicit conflict winner and prevents inline-only traceability.
items.statement: requirement_refs wins conflicts with inline tags, and inline tags cannot stand alone.
items.title: Inline tag conflict rule

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The former DRY Rules source-preserving bridge is retired in place after Phase 2B atomized or structurally dispositioned DRY_Rules-S0001 through DRY_Rules-S0022 into DR-002 through DR-035, explicit structural coverage, and retired bridge lineage. DR-001 remains only as migration lineage for the retired bridge span and must not re-own atomized source coverage.

items.impact: Prevents the historical bridge from competing with atomized units or being compiled into implementation work.
items.statement: DR-001 is retired migration lineage and no longer owns product coverage.
items.title: Source-preserving bridge retired

evidence.exact_quote: - Canonical or implementation-changing unresolved-owner/source mutation blocks, asks, or records a bounded open item.

items.impact: Implementations can choose different outcomes for the same unresolved route, race between asking and recording, or proceed after a partial receipt failure; audit evidence cannot prove consistent enforcement without a selection rule and state-transition oracle.
items.statement: The unresolved-owner states and non-DRY boundaries are explicit, but the choice among block, ask, or bounded-open-item outcomes, transition precedence, concurrent mutation handling, receipt failure behavior, and recovery are not deterministic here.
items.title: Unresolved-owner fallback admits divergent transitions

segments.summary: Reviewed the complete prologue plus DR-002 and DR-003: canonical naming, SSOT consumption, precedence, owner routing, gateable ContractRefs, and the source-preserving PlanUnit boundaries.
Reviewed DR-004 through DR-010 across precedence, owner-first propagation, consumer mirrors, routed identity/runtime concepts, scheduling vocabulary, and graph-record-storage-command ownership.

Reviewed DR-011 through DR-018 across SCM and permission authority, compatibility aliases, recovery/audit routing, projection-backed GUI truth, and stale-event/Crosswalk failures; identified the missing testable projection state machine.

Reviewed DR-019 through DR-026 across corroboration I/O, UI route canon, assistant worktree/chat ownership and traceability, index-only consumers, and forbidden drift patterns; identified missing dispatch-field and lint oracles.

Reviewed DR-027 through DR-034 across ContractRef triggers and taxonomy, semantic packet matching, stable-reference guidance, gate failure, inline-tag authority, and coverage authority; identified normalization collision, non-gateable preference, and pre-node authority gaps.

Reviewed DR-035, retired DR-001 lineage, migration coverage, DR-036 fallback/disabled semantics, and the FABLE repair addendum; identified nondeterministic unresolved-owner transitions while confirming non-DRY authority remains binding.

Does the packet-fidelity owner constrain normalization to prose or detect collisions for whitespace-significant code, tables, YAML, and literals under DR-030?
What is the canonical requirement-coverage state before node shards and derived requirements_coverage.json exist under DR-034?
Which owner selects and orders block, ask, and bounded-open-item outcomes, including concurrent mutations and receipt failures, for DR-036?
